newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Treasury sees no financing changes.
newsitem.headline: Australian Treasury sees no financing changes.

text.p: The Australian Treasury said there had been no revisions to the 1996/97 budget estimates announced on August 20.

The Commonwealth's financing task for 1996/97 was estimated in the budget at A$6.0 billion, comprising secheduled debt repayments of A$5.3 billion and A$1.2 billion of payments associated with public trading enterprise superannuation, partly offset by an estimated headline budget surplus of A$0.5 billion.
"At this stage, there have been no revisions to the 1996/97 budget estimates," said Tony Hinton, First Assistant Secretary, Investment and Debt Division Commwealth Treasury.

Addressing the Australian Financial Markets Association (AFMA) in Sydney, Hinton confirmed that the total borrowing programme for 1996/97 was expected to be around A$7.0 billion, significantly below the levels of recent years.
"The expected net borrowing programme or net call on the markets, which is the total borrowing less maturing debt and early redemptions, is A$0.7 billion, the lowest since 1989/90." Hinton said.
Net borrowings were around A$5.0 billion in 1995/96 and A$14.0 billion in 1994/95.
Hinton said that the expected A$7.0 billion borrowing programme is A$1.0 billion larger that the minimum programme required to meet the budget financing task.
This would provide some flexibility to repurchase in advance Treasury Bonds scheduled for maturity in budget out-years, around one to three years in advance, if this was judged desirable, he added.

"At this stage, it is intended that any repurchases be undertaken from the Reserve Bank's portfolio of Commonwealth Government Securities, rather than directly from the market. Any such redemptions, as usual, will be priced at prevailing market rates," Hinton said.
Net borrowings for 1997/98, 1998/99 and 1999/2000 were projected to be negative, as the value of debt repayments was expected to be greater that the value of new debt issued.
The net borrowing were project at minus A$5.6 billion for 1997/98, minus A$2.5 billion for 1998/99 and minus A$4.7 billion for 1999/2000, Hinton added.
